concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
question:
Which of the following statement is 'true' for ‘dobereiner's triads'?

I. Triads were in order of atomic masses.

II. Atomic mass of middle element was roughly the average of atomic masses of other two elements.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dobereiner's triads were groups of three elements.
 
• The elements in each triad were ordered by their atomic masses.
 
• The atomic mass of the middle element was roughly the average of the atomic masses of the other two elements.
 
• Dobereiner's triads were an early attempt to classify elements based on their properties and atomic masses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dobereiner's Triads**

 
 
• Johann Wolfgang Döbereiner was a German chemist who, in the early 19th century, observed that certain groups of three elements (which he called "triads") had similar chemical properties and that the atomic mass of the middle element was approximately the average of the atomic masses of the other two elements.
 
• Examples of Dobereiner's triads include:
 
 
• Lithium (Li), Sodium (Na), Potassium (K)
 
• Calcium (Ca), Strontium (Sr), Barium (Ba)
 
• Chlorine (Cl), Bromine (Br), Iodine (I)
 
 
 
• Dobereiner's triads were an important step in the development of the periodic table, as they provided early evidence that elements could be grouped based on their properties and atomic masses.
 
• Although Dobereiner's triads were limited to a small number of elements, they paved the way for further classification schemes, eventually leading to Dmitri Mendeleev's periodic table.
